clue.text: Not natural to be attacked

definitions.meaning: put on for show, assumed rather than genuine
struck by a disease, as a crop is said to be hit by blight

explanation.definitionFit: Two separate senses: a mannered, pretentious manner, and being hit or harmed by an illness.

clue.text: Wave that surges through sea, found in branches

indicators.note: one piece goes right through the middle of the other, so it sits inside

parts.note: the Aral Sea in Central Asia
a bore is a tidal wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: A great wave rolls through the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' signals the insertion. 'sea' looks generic but names a particular one, the Aral Sea between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree-dwelling creatures live among the branches, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Without responsibilities or solid means of support?

definitions.text: Without responsibilities or solid means of support?

parts.words: Without responsibilities or solid means of support?
parts.note: fancy-free and unattached, and read literally a foot that is loose gives no firm standing

explanation.definitionFit: Being free to go anywhere with no ties is the idiomatic sense; the second half plays on a wobbly foot.

clue.text: Shrewd move of Nancy's

indicators.note: the letters of the name are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the girl's name, its possessive giving no letter

explanation.surface: A clever tactic played by a woman called Nancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move of' rearranges NANCY.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny is a synonym of shrewd, astute and careful, especially in Scottish use.

clue.text: Well-turned short poem, essential Dante

indicators.note: the word for the poem is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: an elegy is a mournful poem

indicators.note: the essence or core of the poet's name, its middle letters

explanation.surface: A neat little verse capturing the essence of the Italian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims ELEGY to ELEG; 'essential' takes ANT from the middle of DANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-turned phrase or ankle is graceful and stylish, the same sense as the adjective.

clue.text: Keep carrying box

annotationWithheld.why: 'Keep carrying box' as held: CARTON is the box, but no reading of 'Keep carrying' gives the remaining letters; the clue looks cut short in OCR and the scan is unreadable.

clue.text: Painstaking medical procedure?

parts.note: read 'painstaking' as pain-taking: a treatment that takes the pain away

explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is relief from pain, the effect a painkilling treatment produces.

clue.text: Army picking a conscript up in the Russian zone

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pair is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, often a draftee

explanation.surface: An army picks up a recruit somewhere in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AGI into IGA, which follows TA. 'picking' and 'in the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The taiga is the coniferous forest belt across northern Russia, a vegetation zone.

clue.text: Quantity the Romans had in excess?

definitions.text: Quantity the Romans had in excess?

parts.words: Quantity the Romans had in excess?
parts.note: 'excess' sounds like X-C, the Roman numeral for this number

explanation.definitionFit: In Roman numerals XC stands for this number, and 'ex-cess' plays on those letters.

clue.text: Fail to get out saw

definitions.meaning: to be detained or kept in, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word means be detained; whole it is an old past tense of behold, meaning saw.

clue.text: Colour part of eye with end of crayon

parts.note: the brow is the ridge above the eye

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Shading part of the eye with a crayon, as in make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes N from 'crayon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown is simply one of the colours, an earthy shade.

clue.text: Always 50% off, in transport plan

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a transport of joy is elation

indicators.note: half of the word is removed, here its last two letters

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A permanent half-price deal on a transport scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% off' removes half of EVER, and 'in' signals the insertion. 'transport' means rapture, not vehicles, and 'plan' is the architect's drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture an elevation is a drawn plan of one face of a building.

clue.text: Career lay in ruins: having started, one couldn't finish it

definitions.text: having started, one couldn't finish it

indicators.note: the letters lie wrecked and are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A career was wrecked: someone who began could never complete it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ruins' rearranges CAREER LAY. The definition works because each runner starts or finishes only one leg of the team event.
explanation.definitionFit: In a team event each runner covers one leg, so whoever starts it cannot also finish it.

clue.text: Ulysses was Greek, a soldier

parts.note: a soldier ant is a caste of ant that defends the colony

explanation.surface: Ulysses, the hero, was a Greek warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses suggests Homer's Greek hero, but the definition is the American general and president Ulysses S. Grant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S. Grant was the Union general and 18th US president, so his first name points to him.

clue.text: A witticism cracked by teacher about Ovid, for one

indicators.note: the word is broken open and another piece put inside

parts.note: a mot is a witty saying, as in bon mot

indicators.note: turned around, read backwards

parts.note: sir is a schoolchild's name for a male teacher

explanation.surface: A joke told by a teacher concerning the Roman poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the turn, 'cracked by' the insertion. Ovid wrote the Amores and the Ars Amatoria, love poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid wrote the Ars Amatoria and Amores, making him a writer of love poetry, an example of a lover or love poet.

clue.text: In Jim Hawkins' father's line, some name-dropping is appropriate

indicators.note: one N, the abbreviation for name, is dropped from the word

parts.note: in Treasure Island, Jim's father keeps the Admiral Benbow inn, so his trade is running an inn

explanation.surface: Mentioning famous names suits the literary setting of Treasure Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some name-dropping' removes one N (name) from INNKEEPING, leaving IN KEEPING. 'line' means line of business.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in keeping is fitting or suitable for its setting, an idiom for appropriate.

clue.text: Period in which ideology brings consternation

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a day is a period of time
an ism is any doctrine or ideology

explanation.surface: An era when a political creed causes alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' signals the insertion; 'brings' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is a direct synonym of consternation: alarm and distress.

clue.text: Country, in short, is wizard!

parts.note: the country's short name is Oz, the land of the famous wizard

explanation.definitionFit: This country is nicknamed Oz, which shares its name with the Wizard of Oz.

clue.text: Arranges each is to leave prison

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes out of the longer word

parts.note: the Marshalsea was a debtors' prison in Southwark, London

explanation.surface: Organises everyone so that they can be let out of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes EA (each) from MARSHALSEA, the old London debtors' prison in Dickens's Little Dorrit. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal troops or facts is to arrange them in order, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Relent and think about honours

indicators.note: surrounding the next piece

parts.note: ween is an old word for think or suppose
in bridge the ace and king are honour cards, A and K

explanation.surface: Give way and consider the awards you have been given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. In bridge the honours are the top cards, so ace and king give A and K; 'ween' is an archaic verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To weaken is to soften one's resolve or give in a little, which is to relent.

clue.text: Pinched new weapon

parts.note: an arrow is a weapon shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A new weapon has been stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinched' suggests stolen, but it means squeezed thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinched features or a pinched space are tight and thin, the sense of narrow.

clue.text: Is leading each swell of opposition

parts.note: heads means is leading, as in heads the field

explanation.surface: Someone at the front of every wave of protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' is the sea's swell, not a surge of feeling: the definition is nautical.
explanation.definitionFit: A head sea is a swell running directly against a ship's course, so it opposes the vessel.

clue.text: Broke toe — have to stop

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone has fractured a toe and has to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' rearranges TOE and HAVE. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship heaves to by turning into the wind and coming to a halt, the nautical sense of stop.

clue.text: At last, traffic light may appear on road

indicators.note: only the final letter of the next word

parts.note: amber is one of the traffic lights

explanation.surface: Eventually the traffic signal shows on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' gives C, the end of 'traffic'. 'traffic light' reads as one thing, but it splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads are built with a camber, a slight curve so rainwater runs off, so one may be seen on a road.

clue.text: Match with a foreigner broken off

indicators.note: the final letter is snapped off

parts.note: a Greek is a foreigner from a British point of view

explanation.surface: A game against an overseas player is abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken off' trims GREEK to GREE. 'with' is a link word. 'Match' looks like a fixture but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that agree correspond or tally, so they match.

clue.text: Game Boy instructions

parts.note: RU is rugby union
Les is a boy's name, short for Leslie

explanation.surface: The booklet of directions that comes with a handheld games console.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game Boy' reads as the Nintendo console but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rules are the instructions or regulations that govern how something is done.

clue.text: Back what Guardian does?

definitions.meaning: a guardian brings up the children in their charge, read as two words: raises those in care

explanation.definitionFit: As one word it means backwards; split, it describes a guardian raising young people in care.

clue.text: Like the Web? Ladies have a change of heart

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: women means ladies

explanation.surface: Women surfing the internet change their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have a change of heart' replaces M, the centre of WOMEN, with V.
explanation.definitionFit: A web is woven, like cloth or a spider's work, so the adjective describes it.

clue.text: Not like lamb's lettuce stuffed into stomachs endlessly

indicators.note: the lettuce is packed inside the other word
the last letter is cut off

parts.note: bellies are stomachs
cos is a type of lettuce

explanation.surface: Lamb's lettuce used as a stuffing for tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final S and 'stuffed into' signals the insertion. 'Lamb's lettuce' is a real salad green, but here it splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambs are proverbially meek, so being warlike and aggressive is unlike one.

clue.text: House team

definitions.meaning: a large country or holiday residence
Aston ..., the Birmingham football club, is often just called by its last word

explanation.definitionFit: It is a grand residence, and also the short name of an English football club.

clue.text: Succeeded during term of office? This caller thinks not

indicators.note: the letter comes in the middle of the term

parts.note: a monarch's reign is their term on the throne
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a leader succeeded in office, and the person phoning doubts it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts S inside REIGN. The definition replies to the question: someone who calls it a day does not think they will succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to call it a day, judging that carrying on will not bring success.

clue.text: Measures of protection from talons: substance of nail commonly sheathed

indicators.note: the claws enclose the other piece like a sheath

parts.note: talons are claws

indicators.note: a dropped H marks casual speech

parts.note: nails and claws are made of horn

explanation.surface: Protective measures against an animal's talons, the nail tissue being covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' drops the H, as in casual London speech, and 'sheathed' signals the insertion; 'from' is a link word. The Corn Laws were 19th-century British tariffs on imported grain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Corn Laws were protectionist measures keeping grain prices high for British farmers.
